subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A random variable X has the following probability distribution: X = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; P(X = xᵢ) = k, 2k, 3k, 4k, 5k. Find k and the mean and variance of X.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find k, the mean and the variance from a probability table — what equation gives k, and what you multiply and add for the mean and for the variance.
insider_note: The first two marks are for the equation Σ P(X = xᵢ) = 1 written out, not for k = 1/15 alone; and the variance subtracts μ², so the mean 11/3 has to be found before it.

steps.label: Find k
steps.margin_note: First two marks. Every probability distribution has one rule: the probabilities add to 1. Write the table, write ΣP(X = xᵢ) = 1, add the k's — 15k = 1 gives k = 1/15. Keep k as a fraction; the mean and variance are found in k first and 1/15 is put in at the end.
steps.memory_tip: Add the PROBABILITIES, not the values: 15k = 1. Write the ΣP = 1 line — the equation is the mark.

recall.must_convey: That the probabilities add to 1, so k + 2k + 3k + 4k + 5k = 15k = 1 and k = 1/15.
accept: the probabilities add up to one so fifteen k equals one and k is one by fifteen
sum of P of X equals one gives fifteen k equal to one
add all the k terms, set the sum to one, k comes to one over fifteen
anni probabilities kalipithe one, so fifteen k equals one, k is one by fifteen
use sigma P equals one to get k

steps.why: A random variable's probabilities must add to 1 because X takes exactly one of the listed values in every trial. That one equation is the only place the table gives you information about k.
common_mistakes: Adding the x-values (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5) instead of the probabilities.
Never writing ΣP(X = xᵢ) = 1 before solving — the examiner marks the equation, not only the value.

steps.label: Find the mean
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Mean μ = Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ): multiply each value by its probability and add. Factor the k out — k(1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25) = 55k — and only then put k = 1/15. 55/15 simplifies to 11/3; leave it as a fraction.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply each value by its probability and factor k out: k(1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25) = 55k = 11/3.

recall.must_convey: That the mean is Σxᵢ·P(X = xᵢ) = 55k = 55/15 = 11/3.
accept: mean is sigma x times P of x which is fifty five k so eleven by three
multiply each value by its probability and add to get eleven by three
mu equals sum of x i P x i, comes to fifty five by fifteen
prathi x ni daani probability tho multiply chesi add cheste mean eleven by three
the mean is fifty five k which is eleven by three

steps.why: The mean is a weighted average: each value counts as much as its probability. Factoring k out keeps the arithmetic in whole numbers until the last line, which is where most slips are avoided.
common_mistakes: Adding the probabilities to the values instead of multiplying.
Putting k = 1/15 into every term first and then adding five fractions.

steps.label: Find the variance
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Variance σ² = Σxᵢ²·P(X = xᵢ) − μ². Square each VALUE (not the probability), multiply by its probability, add — k(1 + 8 + 27 + 64 + 125) = 225k = 15 — then subtract μ² = 121/9. The answer 14/9 is positive, as a variance must be.
steps.memory_tip: Square the VALUES, not the probabilities: k(1 + 8 + 27 + 64 + 125) = 15, then subtract μ² = 121/9.

recall.must_convey: That the variance is Σxᵢ²·P(X = xᵢ) − μ² = 225k − (11/3)² = 15 − 121/9 = 14/9.

steps.why: Variance measures how far the values sit from the mean on average, so it needs the squares of the values and the mean together. The formula Σxᵢ²P − μ² is the same as Σ(xᵢ − μ)²P but far quicker with a fraction for μ.
common_mistakes: Squaring the probabilities instead of the values.
Getting a negative variance and not stopping — a negative variance always means an arithmetic slip.
